description.p: Beta. holzWave is a terminal emulator written from scratch in Rust, with tiled panes and a layout that is restored on the next start. This is an early preview: this Flatpak was built in a container and has never been started on a Linux desktop, so how it behaves on GNOME, KDE Plasma and the other desktops is not known.

Panes start in the sandbox by default. A terminal in a sandbox sees only the runtime's tools and none of yours, so this Flatpak also ships the permission to run commands on the host (flatpak-spawn --host, the permission org.freedesktop.Flatpak). Using it is your choice: you can switch it on in Settings, in the group Host shell. It is off by default and is never synced to another computer. With it on, new panes start your login shell on the host, outside the sandbox and with your rights. Because the permission is shipped, the sandbox does not protect the rest of your system from this application, whatever the setting says. If you remove the permission with a Flatpak tool, the setting reads not available and panes stay in the sandbox.

It also asks for your home folder; for the SSH agent socket (--socket=ssh-auth), because the built-in SSH client signs in with the keys in your agent; and for the Secret Service on the session bus (--talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets), because the passwords, passphrases and provider keys it keeps live in the system keychain and never in a file. Neither costs more sandbox than the permission to run commands on the host already does.

holzWave also asks for the network (--share=network). It uses it for the SSH connections you start, for the sync you set up and, for the AI chat, for the messages you send to a provider you set up. It connects to nothing when it starts on a fresh install, and it has no telemetry, no account and no update check. A pane in the sandbox uses the network of the app, a pane on the host uses the host's network.

The integrations (the Kubernetes, Talos, Azure CLI and GAM7 blocks) are not available in a Flatpak. The directory of a pane on the host is tracked only when the shell announces it. Whether a host shell has job control and sudo, whether the SSH agent and the keychain work through the sandbox, and how the window looks on each desktop have not been tested.
Preview release. The terminal engine moved to Ghostty 1.4 and keeps all the scrollback lines it is given. The Linux packages were built on a runner and have not been started on a desktop.
